Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this on. Attaching our current MSA and an Exhibit A (party sheet) — both are early drafts. We're trying to get contracting wrapped up in the next three weeks so we can hit our launch window.

Key asks up front:
- Can Redwood confirm which template we'll be on (standard MSA + Order Form)?
- Who will steward Exhibit A updates from your side?
- Any non-starter clauses up front (data residency, indemnity caps)?

Attached: MSA_v1_MSFlow_draft.docx, ExhibitA_party_sheet.csv.

Eric

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Eric Tan <eric.tan@msaflow.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — initial intake + timeline

Hi Eric — thanks for sending these over and for the proposed timeline. Looping in Laura (contracts lead) and Jordan (account exec) to pick up scope and signatory coordination.

High level from our side:
- We typically use Redwood Standard MSA + separate Order Form for commercial terms. If there are no bespoke privacy or residency asks we can usually stay on template.
- Stewardship: Laura will be the contracting steward for this agreement — she'll own clause-level redlines and interface with your legal ops. Jordan will track billing/contact updates and signatures.

Quick requests to help us triage:
1) Please confirm the primary billing contact and the signatory (name, title, email) for the Order Form.
2) Can you mark any clauses in your MSA that you expect to be negotiated (we find a quick rubric helps prioritize)?
3) Do you require any SOC2 / audit artifacts for procurement? If so, please list the specific artifacts and a point of contact.

I'll attach our intake checklist (internal) to speed handoff — it covers party mapping, data residency, encryption/KMS, and SLAs.

Proposed next steps:
- Laura will circulate a redline plan by 2026-06-11.
- We aim to return a marked-up MSA within 3 business days of that plan (target 2026-06-14).

If that timeline works, we'll treat the 2026-06-18 redline exchange as the formal milestone.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: contracting-intake-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Eric Tan <eric.tan@msaflow.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-11T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — initial intake + timeline

Stephanie / Eric — taking the steward lead here. Quick read-through notes and plan below.

On Tue, Jun 9, 2026 at 09:12, Eric Tan <eric.tan@msaflow.com> wrote:
> Hi Stephanie,
> 
> Thanks for taking this on. Attaching our current MSA and an Exhibit A (party sheet) — both are early drafts. We're trying to get contracting wrapped up in the next three weeks so we can hit our launch window.

Summary of priority flags from our first pass:
- Data residency: MSAFlow has references to EU-only processing for customer data in Exhibit A; we need to confirm whether Redwood can commit to region-specific hosting for that workload.
- Liability / cap: their draft removes caps for certain breach scenarios — we'll propose a balanced cap tied to fees with carveouts for gross negligence.
- Indemnities: there are reciprocal indemnities that are non-standard for our template; we'll preserve customer-friendly language but propose clearer trigger events.

Plan & deliverables:
1) I'll produce a redline plan (short doc) by 2026-06-11 with section-by-section priorities and rationale.
2) After alignment with Stephanie and Jordan, I'll generate a marked-up MSA (tracked changes) and an annotated Exhibit A by 2026-06-14.
3) If MSAFlow can provide the final signatory info and billing contact by EOD 2026-06-12, we can keep the 06-18 exchange milestone.

Attachment: redline-outline.md (simple checklist + clause map) — includes clause IDs to watch, recommended language snippets, and a risk score for each ask.

Questions for Eric:
- Does the Exhibit A party sheet reflect production-region requirements per-customer or per-tenant? (We need to know whether the residency requirement is contract-level or account-level.)
- Any third-party subprocessor lists you can share? That speeds security vetting.

Thanks — I'll follow up after the plan is posted.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Contracts & Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline-outline.md (txt)
